convention/PRPKG24-BOUNDED-PDF-MEASURE-0.source_reading: The phrase 'D has pdf f_D' is represented by a probability measure equal to Lebesgue volume with density ofReal(f_D), with f_D nonnegative, measurable, and integrable. The Theorem 1(ii) allocation endpoint additionally adopts an a.e. nonnegative conditional-value convention. Given that convention, its lower endpoint L, positive width, and positive M are support normalizations rather than separate claims about every merely upper-bounded translated law.

convention/PRPKG24-COMMON-MEAN-SIGN-01.source_reading: For the all-consumed common-distribution endpoint, the common conditional mean is nonnegative for the weak argmax direction and positive for the unique argmax direction.

convention/PRPKG24-POSITIVE-PREFERENCE-S.source_reading: For the checked fixed-k gamma-share endpoints that assert a limiting representation for every named type, the source-selected preferred-type PMF has strictly positive mass at every type. This is an additional regularity condition on the all-coordinate route, not a claim that the archival model text excluded zero-probability types.

convention/PRPKG24-THEOREM2-INDEPENDENT-.source_reading: For each type and finite count, the rank coordinates are independent Boolean variables with rank-specific success parameter c*((i+1)+d)^(-alpha). They are not asserted iid across ranks; cross-type independence is neither asserted nor needed because one preferred type is evaluated.

defect/PRPKG24-COROLLARY3-QONE-OPTIMALIT.source_reading: Corollary 3 assumes q>0 and concludes that every top-one optimal sequence is asymptotically uniform. The stated domain includes q=1. With at least two positively likely types and q=1, every allocation that gives each such type at least one item already has top-one success probability one, so nonuniform optimal sequences exist.

defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD1-GENERIC-ASYMPTOTI.memo_heading: Theorem 1 and Appendix Lemma D.1 share asymptotics
defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD1-GENERIC-ASYMPTOTI.source_reading: The single named lemma asserts four generic optimizer-share limits from nonnegative weights and asymptotics of h, then its proof uses every coordinate's divergence to infinity and a limiting compact optimization argument. Its proof divides through min_i p_i despite allowing zeros; case (ii) turns a deficit ratio into a strict objective-value ratio although both objectives approach A sum p; and case (iii) labels the required log-objective maximum a minimum.

defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD1-II-OBJECTIVE-RATI.memo_heading: Theorem 1 and Appendix Lemma D.1 share asymptotics
defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD1-II-OBJECTIVE-RATI.source_reading: After proving a strict ratio comparison of the saturation deficits A-h(a), the proof concludes that the ratio of the original objective values is strictly below one in Equation (61).

defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD1-III-MAX-DIRECTION.memo_heading: Theorem 1 and Appendix Lemma D.1 share asymptotics
defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD1-III-MAX-DIRECTION.source_reading: The proof says that sum_t p_t log(x_t) has a unique minimum at the target shares, while its preceding strict inequality and the correct entropy calculation require a unique maximum.

defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD1-SIGN-01.memo_heading: Theorem 1 and Appendix Lemma D.1 share asymptotics
defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD1-SIGN-01.source_reading: Lemma D.1(i) assumes A,B>0 and sigma<0 while concluding uniform shares from log(A-h(a))/(B a^sigma) -> 1. This is false as written even for positive normalized weights: m=2, p=(1/4,3/4), h(a)=1-1/(a+1), A=2, B=1, sigma=-1 satisfies the displayed limit but has square-root rather than uniform optimizer shares.

defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD3-SCALE-CONSTANT-01.source_reading: For an exponential distribution with rate lambda, Lemma D.3 prints mu_D(a-i,a) - log a - B(i) -> 0 for a positive constant B(i), and calls the sequence strictly concave without stating the valid-rank domain.

defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD4-PDF-RANK-DOMAIN-0.source_reading: Lemma D.4 calls x^(-alpha-1) a Pareto PDF for alpha > 1, omitting its alpha normalizer, and asserts strict concavity over a totalized fixed-rank order-statistic expression without a valid-rank/eventual domain.

defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD5-CONCAVITY-REGULAR.source_reading: Lemma D.5 prints strictly convex summands while maximizing their sum, but Equation 197 and the marginal comparison in Equations 194-195 require concavity; the proof also invokes partial derivatives without stating differentiability.

defect/PRPKG24-LEMMAD5-GENERAL-ROUNDING-.source_reading: Lemma D.5 claims that an optimal nonnegative integer solution of a separable fixed-sum problem lies within m coordinates of an optimal nonnegative real solution.

defect/PRPKG24-PROP2-FINITE-CONSTANT-01.memo_heading: Proposition 2 and the finite uniform model
defect/PRPKG24-PROP2-FINITE-CONSTANT-01.source_reading: Proposition 2 prints the finite representation error bound (m+1)/n, while the displayed relaxed optimizer and rounding argument yield the corrected bound (2m+1)/n.

defect/PRPKG24-PROP4-CONTINUITY-BOUNDARY.source_reading: The source assumes only a nonconstant radial probability kernel, but the pointwise-supremum Laplace identity needs regularity excluding isolated measure-zero payoff spikes.

defect/PRPKG24-PROP4-EQ18-TYPE-01.source_reading: Equation 18 prints Gamma(pi) as an element of inf_alpha Gamma(alpha), although both sides are real-valued; the intended claim is that the uniform profile attains the infimum.

defect/PRPKG24-PROP4-EQ20-MEASURE-OMISSI.source_reading: Equation 20 changes the finite-n integral from the preference-weighted measure in Equation 17 to bare surface measure as a displayed equality. Full support preserves the limiting Laplace rate, not the finite-n integral itself.

defect/PRPKG24-THEOREM1I-NONDEGENERATE-T.source_reading: Theorem 1(i) says every finite discrete D gives an all-type uniform limiting representation for arbitrary optimal sets.

defect/PRPKG24-THEOREM1V-NEGATIVE-MEAN-D.source_reading: Theorem 1 assumes only that the common iid conditional-value law has finite mean, then says that the all-consumed optimum uses a type maximizing p_t. A negative common mean reverses that direction: the all-consumed expected value of an item of type t is p_t times the common mean.

defect/PRPKG24-THEOREM2-RANK-VARYING-IID.source_reading: The Theorem 2 header calls X_i^(t) iid Bernoulli while prescribing the rank-dependent parameter q_i = c(i+d)^(-alpha). It also permits c=0 and a first-rank success probability of one although the top-one universal-optimizer conclusions become flat or tie-degenerate there.

defect/PRPKG24-THEOREM3-ENDPOINT-DOMAIN-.source_reading: Theorem 3 prints the all-type share weight 1 / log(1 / (1-q_t)) for Bernoulli(q_t) conditional values without excluding q_t=0 or q_t=1. At q_t=0 the denominator is zero, and at q_t=1 the displayed real-valued expression is not a finite defined share weight.
